member.name: T:AgentsPoker.Core.ActionType
member.summary:
The only decision an agent makes (TDD Part 1 §2). The agent expresses an INTENT; the engine turns it into chips.
: give up the hand (a FOLD with nothing to call is a real fold unless is set).
: match the current bet; with nothing owed it is a CHECK. If the stack is too short it is an all-in call.
: with no bet yet it is a BET; otherwise a raise of exactly one fixed increment (20 preflop/flop, 40 turn/river). If raising is not legal it is downgraded to CALL (see ). With fewer chips than a full raise it is an all-in for less.
Names match the TDD contract exactly. Any other numeric value is treated as invalid (CHECK if free, else FOLD).

member.name: T:AgentsPoker.Core.TableMatch
member.summary:
Bracket table helper (TDD Part 2 §1): fixed number of hands (30), same starting stack, top N by stack advance. Headless. The Unity Arena should drive it one hand at a time with (not Table.PlayHand directly), so the stack history used by the tie-break is recorded.
Ranking: higher final stack first. Equal stacks: compare stacks after the previous hand, then the one before, ... back to the starting stacks; the first hand where they differ decides (higher was better more recently). Still equal: lower seat index. Deterministic, and busted players who busted later rank higher.

member.name: T:AgentsPoker.Core.HandEvaluator
member.summary:
Fast 5/6/7-card Hold'em evaluator based on 13-bit rank masks + precomputed lookup tables (straight-high table, bit-count and highest-bit tables, 8192 entries each). No allocation per call, no per-combination if/else: a 7-card hand is evaluated directly (no 21 five-card sub-hands). Tens of ns per 7-card hand.
Value contract (stable, the swap point of the SDK): an int where HIGHER = BETTER; equal values = exact tie (split). Layout: category (bits 20..23) | up to 5 rank nibbles (bits 0..19, ranks 2..14). Only comparisons, , and are part of the contract; do not decode the nibbles yourself.
vs Cactus Kev / TwoPlusTwo (TDD Part 1 §1): same idea (lookup tables, no big if/else trees) with a tiny memory footprint (~24 KB instead of Cactus Kev's prime-product tables or TwoPlusTwo's ~130 MB state table). It produces exactly the 7462 distinct 5-card equivalence classes of Cactus Kev, and returns Cactus Kev's numbering (1 = royal flush ... 7462 = 7-5-4-3-2 offsuit), verified exhaustively by the test suite over all 2,598,960 5-card and all 133,784,560 7-card hands. If ever needed, the internals can be swapped for a TwoPlusTwo table without changing this API.
